changelog_entries.derivation: Reproduced from Atlassian's own published Jira Cloud REST API v3 documentation examples for this endpoint: the field names, nesting and value formats are the documented ones, with synthetic values (acme.atlassian.net, the ABC project, Atlassian's own example-style accountIds). Avatar URL maps and email addresses that appear in the published examples are omitted, because no normalizer reads them and a committed fixture should not carry contact details at all. This is therefore evidence that the shape is the *documented* one and is NOT evidence that the live API still matches it: documentation drifts from implementations, api.atlassian.com is unreachable from this environment, and no response was recorded. `lltpm integrations verify` reports it as unverifiable rather than passing. The entries cover every changelog item class the normalizer decides about: a status transition, a priority and due-date change saved together in one entry, an assignee change (accountId in `to`, display name in `toString`), a Link change, a time-spent and worklog pair, a Sprint custom field, and a resolution plus status pair.

Two pages, because one page cannot exercise pagination: the first carries a nextPageToken with isLast false, the second omits the token and sets isLast true. This is the shape most likely to have drifted and the first thing to re-verify once egress exists.
search_pages.endpoint_note: The token-paginated enhanced search. The offset-paginated GET /rest/api/3/search is deprecated on Jira Cloud and is deliberately not used.

webhooks.derivation: Reproduced from Atlassian's own published Jira Cloud REST API v3 documentation examples for this endpoint: the field names, nesting and value formats are the documented ones, with synthetic values (acme.atlassian.net, the ABC project, Atlassian's own example-style accountIds). Avatar URL maps and email addresses that appear in the published examples are omitted, because no normalizer reads them and a committed fixture should not carry contact details at all. This is therefore evidence that the shape is the *documented* one and is NOT evidence that the live API still matches it: documentation drifts from implementations, api.atlassian.com is unreachable from this environment, and no response was recorded. `lltpm integrations verify` reports it as unverifiable rather than passing. Three deliveries: an issue_updated carrying both the issue and the changelog entry that caused it, a comment_created, and a worklog_updated that the normalizer declines to interpret. Note that no delivery here is signed: a signature is computed over raw bytes in the webhook tests rather than stored, since a committed fixture must not carry a secret.
webhooks.endpoint: GET /rest/api/3/webhook (delivery body shape; nothing in this repository hosts a receiver yet)

note: Jira Cloud REST v3 payloads for offline contract tests. Every file here has provenance 'official_documentation': it follows the shape Atlassian publishes for the endpoint, with synthetic values, and nothing was recorded from a live site — the network policy in this environment cannot reach api.atlassian.com or any *.atlassian.net host. That is weaker than a recording and stronger than a hand-written mock, and it is labelled as exactly that: calling one of these 'recorded' would claim a live check that never happened.
